Traditional Spiced Ale

Served at: Twelfth Night · St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day)

Serves 6Prep 10 minCook 15 min

Spiced Ale is a warm, aromatic beverage traditionally served during Twelfth Night and St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day) celebrations in many English-speaking countries. It combines ale with a blend of spices and citrus, symbolizing the festive spirit and the end of the Christmas season.

Ingredients

  • 6 cups (1.4 liters) dark ale or stout
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) brown sugar
  • 1 orange, sliced
  • 1 lemon, sliced
  • 4 whole cloves
  • 2 cinnamon sticks
  • 2 star anise
  • 1/2 teaspoon grated nutmeg
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger

Method

  1. Pour the ale into a large saucepan and warm over low heat, avoiding boiling.
  2. Add the brown sugar, orange slices, lemon slices, cloves, cinnamon sticks, star anise, nutmeg, and ground ginger to the ale.
  3. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes to allow the flavors to infuse, stirring occasionally to dissolve the sugar.
  4. Remove from heat and strain the ale to remove the spices and citrus slices.
  5. Ladle the spiced ale into heatproof mugs or glasses and serve warm.

Tips

  • Use a good quality dark ale or stout for a richer flavor.
  • Adjust the sweetness by adding more or less brown sugar to taste.
  • For a non-alcoholic version, substitute the ale with apple cider or a spiced black tea.
